overview: Session 16 is the long run of production, when both capital and labor can change. An isoquant shows every input mix that makes the same output, and the MRTS is its slope: how much capital one more worker replaces. The isocost line shows every mix that costs the same. The cheapest way to make a target output is where they touch, which gives the bang-for-the-buck rule MP_L/w = MP_K/r. When an input's price changes, the firm substitutes toward the cheaper input. The professor will ask you to find an isocost and the MRTS, compare marginal product per dollar, and find the cost-minimizing mix by hand. The sheet has MRTS = MP_L/MP_K and the isocost slope -w/r; the cost-minimizing rule itself must be memorized.
